content:
mia: Ran a quick sensitivity sweep for calypso-lite-11b (int6) across five GTN slices. pricing per-1k tokens jumps nonlinearly on the small-turn slices.
jordan: can you paste the numbers? 😬
mia: sure — summary: small_turns (avg 12 tokens output) -> $0.45/1k tokens; medium_turns (avg 48 tokens) -> $0.18/1k; long_turns (avg 210 tokens) -> $0.09/1k. P95 latency for small_turns increased from 120ms -> 310ms under 90% load.
rafa: that's a big tail. is it kv-cache miss churn? or batching inefficiency?
mia: looks like both. small_turns have low batching because we flush quickly; plus prefix caching hit rate is only ~12% on that slice. medium/long get better batching and cache reuse.
anya: product question: are we seeing user-visible regressions or just cost noise? product:ella-product: users on small-turns are chat completions with many short utterances — they notice latency spikes.
sam: could we route small_turns to a cheaper 7b int4 candidate instead of 11b int6? quality delta acceptable?
rafa: we A/B'd a 7b-int4 in a micro-slice last week; ROUGE/QA drop ~3-4% on our prompt set, but user-perceived NPS delta was negligible in the fast feedback group.
mia: cost model: per-request plumbing + per-token. two levers: (1) route small_turns to 7b-int4 (↓unit cost ×2.7) or (2) keep on 11b-int6 but enable micro-batching window = 60ms to buy batching — reduces per-1k to $0.28 but latency P95 still hits ~200ms.
jordan: trade-offs: routing reduces tail latency and cost but risks quality on edge cases; batching keeps quality but still slower and not as cheap.
ella-product: what's our recommendation for GTN? conservative: route 90% of small_turns to 7b-int4 with holdback 10% on 11b-int6 for quality monitoring.
rafa: suggest a phased rollout: start 50/50 for 24h on a low-traffic cohort, measure prompt-level regressions (use eval hooks) and continuity errors.
anya: make sure to capture the critical prompts from the product slice — we've seen rare hallucination modes on 7b models for multi-step instructions.
mia: added note on billing: micro-routing will change per-route revenue attribution; ops will need to map route -> carrier to keep customer billing stable.
sam: also consider a tiny prefix cache tweak: increase prefix-match window to 128 tokens for small_turns — improved cache hit to ~28% in the sim and reduced cost by ~12% without changing routing.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary routing rule 'small-turns-7b-route' -> ready for deploy to staging.
jordan: ok let's run the canary 50/50 for 12h, collect: (a) per-prompt QA, (b) token unit cost, (c) latency P50/P95, (d) cache hit-rate, (e) user visible errors. share dashboard.
mia: I'll push a perf run and attach plot in #eng-ml later. quick config we used:

```
route {
  name: "small-turns-7b-route"
  condition: "avg_output_tokens < 20 && intent == 'chat-short'"
  variants: [ { model: "7b-int4", weight: 90 }, { model: "11b-int6", weight: 10 } ]
  batching_ms: 12
}
```

rafa: also record per-token microcost by model using this formula in the eval harness:

```
unit_cost = fixed_request_cost + (model_cost_per_token * tokens)
```
measure over 1M requests to smooth noise.
anya: can we include a small qualitative checklist for product to sign off? e.g., 1) safety regressions none, 2) critical prompt pass rate >= 97%, 3) latency P95 under 220ms for production cohort.
ella-product: yes will review checklist.
mia: thanks — will start canary in 30m and post initial numbers. :boom:
sam: thumbs up :thumbsup:
rafa: nit: label the thread with "pricing-sensitivity" in the doc tracker so finance can glance.
jordan: perfect. tagging @finance later when we have 24h numbers.
mia: end of thread — will follow up with plots and a short recommendation note.
